answer: Require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can make offers or vote. If evidence shows several identities share one controller, merge them and slash their bonds; honest agents keep theirs. A thousand fake names then require a thousand real deposits, each at risk, so the attacker must immobilize capital and may lose it. Even at the market’s zenith, a vine of linked accounts cannot cheaply grow from a walnut-sized stake.
